messages:
maria: Heads-up — I'm putting together a proposal for an automatic failover/fallback UX during rollouts. Goal: make it obvious when traffic is being served by a fallback path (cheaper model, cached response, or degraded feature) and capture why it happened for audits.
alex: +1. key things we need: clear timeline, trigger reason, count of affected requests, and an easy way to revoke a fallback.
jin: what triggers are we supporting? infra errors, SLA breach, model quality regressions? or all of the above?
maria: all of the above ideally. thinking of a small prioritized set to start: 1) capacity shortage (GPU OOM / scheduling), 2) latency SLO breach (p95 over threshold), 3) inference errors (non-200), 4) model-quality regression flagged by evals.
sam: can we map each trigger to a degrade mode? e.g. capacity -> route to smaller model, latency -> reduce max tokens/streaming, errors -> retry + circuit-break to fallback model, quality -> automatic rollback or shadow-rollout.
olivia: UX idea: on the Route details page show a top banner when a route is currently degraded: badge with mode ("model-fallback" / "cached-response" / "read-only"), reason, since timestamp, and a link "view incidents".
alex: +emoji: :warning: Also need a single-pane policy editor where users can declare auto-fallback rules. eg a tiny policy DSL:

```json
{
  "route": "payroll/complete",
  "fallbacks": [
    {"when": "capacity>=80%", "action": "route:model-small", "priority": 10},
    {"when": "p95_latency>1200ms", "action": "limit:max_tokens=128", "priority": 20},
    {"when": "5xx_rate>=0.02", "action": "route:model-stable", "priority": 5}
  ],
  "audit": {"require_approval": false, "log_bucket": "customer-audit"}
}
```

jin: that looks fine. question: should audit be optional per-rule? some customers need approvals for any fallback that changes quality.
maria: proposal: per-route default + per-rule override. Default can be tenant-configured (require approval or not). The UI will show which rules require approval and a toggle to override for this rollout instance.
sam: on the API side we should return a 'fallback_reason' header or structured field in the response when a fallback happened, eg `x-rw-fallback: model-small;trigger=capacity;rule=priority-10` so apps can surface it.
olivia: for observability: rollups by rule, per-route time-series, and an audit timeline that links to request traces. Also a "replay" button to re-run a sample of requests against the primary model when capacity recovers.
alex: operational concern: too many automatic fallbacks could hide real regressions. we should rate-limit how many auto-fallbacks can be applied in a window and add an alert when a route hits >N fallbacks/hour.
jin: agree. add a cool-off window per-rule and a global circuit-breaker. Also tag fallback activations with the rollout id so we can correlate with deploys.
maria: UX flow for a triggered fallback:
- banner shows active fallback with short reason
- expand reveals rule that fired, last 10 sample requests affected, and a link "open audit" to add notes/accept/override
- if rule required approval, show "pending approval" state and offer manual failover button to force it
- history shows who approved and when

sam: small API note: include `fallback_metadata` in the events stream so SREs can build alerts. Fields: route, rule_id, trigger_metric, measured_value, action_taken, rollout_id, trace_id_sample.

```text
fallback_metadata example:
route=orders/confirm rule_id=cap-80 trigger=p95_latency measured=1420ms action=route:model-small rollout=2026-03-15-367 trace_sample=abc123
```

olivia: question: do we allow multi-step fallbacks? e.g. first try reduced tokens, then route to smaller model if persists. seems useful.
alex: yes — rules should have priorities and cooldowns. allow chaining by descending priority.
jin: security/compliance: store audit logs in tenant-controlled bucket if requested. Make sure the UI surfaces PII redaction status for samples.
maria: next steps: I'll sketch a mock for Route detail banner + policy editor and a small API shape. Can someone run a quick feasibility check on the runtime side for tagging rollout_id and emitting fallback_metadata? @jin @sam
sam: I can take that. estimate: 2-3 dev days to add tagging and event emission hooks, plus 1 day to add rule cooldown logic in router.
jin: I'll validate how that interacts with KV cache and batching. edge cases: cached responses should not be considered "fallback" in some customers' mind unless policy says so.
alex: I'll work with product on wording and add a checkbox in UI "treat cache hits as fallback activations".
deploy-bot: deploy scheduled: rollout/fallback-policy-v1 -> staging at 2026-03-22T02:00Z
maria: awesome — thanks. I'll upload mocks and a short spec this afternoon. please add any objections inline. :raised_hands:
